title: An hour to kill
setting: A weekday afternoon. Kenji hurt himself at football practice, so Okaasan left work early to take him to the local clinic. They've already waited a while when the receptionist says there's about another hour to go, and that they're free to wait outside.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, mada ichijikan mo kakaru no?
lines.ja: え、まだ一時間もかかるの？
lines.kana: え、まだいちじかんもかかるの？
lines.english: What? It's going to be another whole hour?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: shouganai no yo. koko no sensei, hitori hitori chanto jikan kakete mite kureru kara.
lines.ja: しょうがないのよ。ここの先生、一人一人ちゃんと時間かけて診てくれるから。
lines.kana: しょうがないのよ。ここのせんせい、ひとりひとりちゃんとじかんかけてみてくれるから。
lines.english: It can't be helped. The doctor here takes his time and looks at every patient properly.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: jikan kakesugi da yo. koko de ichijikan mo matsu no, muri.
lines.ja: 時間かけすぎだよ。ここで一時間も待つの、無理。
lines.kana: じかんかけすぎだよ。ここでいちじかんもまつの、むり。
lines.english: He takes way too long. No way am I waiting here a whole hour.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: jaa, mae no kafe de jikan tsubusou ka.
lines.ja: じゃあ、前のカフェで時間潰そうか。
lines.kana: じゃあ、まえのかふぇでじかんつぶそうか。
lines.english: Then shall we kill time at the café across the road?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ii ne. nanika tabenagara jikan tsubusou.
lines.ja: いいね。何か食べながら時間潰そう。
lines.kana: いいね。なにかたべながらじかんつぶそう。
lines.english: Sounds good. Let's eat something while we kill time.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mou futatsume? kega shiteru noni, yoku taberu ne.
lines.ja: もう二つ目？怪我してるのに、よく食べるね。
lines.kana: もうふたつめ？けがしてるのに、よくたべるね。
lines.english: Your second one already? For someone who's hurt, you've got quite an appetite.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: datte hiru, chotto shika tabetenai n da mon. okaasan wa, shigoto daijoubu datta no?
lines.ja: だって昼、ちょっとしか食べてないんだもん。お母さんは、仕事大丈夫だったの？
lines.kana: だってひる、ちょっとしかたべてないんだもん。おかあさんは、しごとだいじょうぶだったの？
lines.english: Well, I hardly ate at lunch. Mum, was it OK to leave work?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: un. konshuu wa isogashii kedo, nantoka jikan tsukutta no.
lines.ja: うん。今週は忙しいけど、なんとか時間作ったの。
lines.kana: うん。こんしゅうはいそがしいけど、なんとかじかんつくったの。
lines.english: Yes. It's a busy week, but I managed to make time.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: itsumo shigoto bakkari de, kenji to yukkuri hanasu jikan, nakanaka torenai shi ne.
lines.ja: いつも仕事ばっかりで、ケンジとゆっくり話す時間、なかなか取れないしね。
lines.kana: いつもしごとばっかりで、けんじとゆっくりはなすじかん、なかなかとれないしね。
lines.english: I'm always working, and I hardly ever get the time to sit and talk with you.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: sokka. nanka, jikan totte kurete arigatou.
lines.ja: そっか。なんか、時間取ってくれてありがとう。
lines.kana: そっか。なんか、じかんとってくれてありがとう。
lines.english: Oh. Um... thanks for making time for me.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: nani yo, kyuu ni. demo, ureshii wa.
lines.ja: 何よ、急に。でも、うれしいわ。
lines.kana: なによ、きゅうに。でも、うれしいわ。
lines.english: What's this, all of a sudden? But it makes me happy.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: a, demo honne iu to, kaeritai. nanka mou itakunai shi.
lines.ja: あ、でも本音言うと、帰りたい。なんかもう痛くないし。
lines.kana: あ、でもほんねいうと、かえりたい。なんかもういたくないし。
lines.english: Oh, but honestly? I want to go home. It sort of doesn't hurt any more.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: dame. sekkaku jikan tsukutta n da kara, chanto sensei ni mite moratte kara kaeru no.
lines.ja: だめ。せっかく時間作ったんだから、ちゃんと先生に診てもらってから帰るの。
lines.kana: だめ。せっかくじかんつくったんだから、ちゃんとせんせいにみてもらってからかえるの。
lines.english: No. I went to the trouble of making time, so we're going home after the doctor's had a proper look.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, jaa raishuu mo kite tte iwaretara?
lines.ja: え、じゃあ来週も来てって言われたら？
lines.kana: え、じゃあらいしゅうもきてっていわれたら？
lines.english: What? Then what if he tells me to come back next week too?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: raishuu nara, mata jikan tsukureru kara daijoubu.
lines.ja: 来週なら、また時間作れるから大丈夫。
lines.kana: らいしゅうなら、またじかんつくれるからだいじょうぶ。
lines.english: Next week I can make time again, so that's fine.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: jaa, mou hitotsu tabete, jikan tsubusou kana.
lines.ja: じゃあ、もう一つ食べて、時間潰そうかな。
lines.kana: じゃあ、もうひとつたべて、じかんつぶそうかな。
lines.english: OK, then maybe I'll kill some time with one more.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. kondo wa jikan kakete, yukkuri taberu.
lines.ja: うん。今度は時間かけて、ゆっくり食べる。
lines.kana: うん。こんどはじかんかけて、ゆっくりたべる。
lines.english: Yep. This time I'll take my time and eat it slowly.

questions.english: What happens while Kenji and Okaasan wait to see the doctor?

choices.english: Okaasan couldn't get away from work, so Kenji waited for the doctor on his own.
With an hour to wait, they killed time at a café. Kenji said it didn't hurt any more and wanted to go home, but Okaasan said he'd see the doctor first, since she'd made the time.
They gave up on the wait and went home, and Okaasan will make time to bring Kenji back next week.

questions.explanation: Line 1: there's still an hour to wait (mada ichijikan mo kakaru). In lines 4-5 they go to the café across the road to kill time. Line 8: Okaasan managed to make time in a busy week. In line 12 Kenji says it doesn't hurt any more and he wants to go home. In line 13 she says no: sekkaku jikan tsukutta n da kara, the doctor looks at it first. A is wrong: Okaasan is right there with him and says she made the time (line 8). C is wrong: she won't go home (line 13). Next week only comes up in case the doctor asks Kenji to come back (lines 14-15).

questions.english: Okaasan explains why the wait is so long. What does she say about the doctor?
questions.ja: お母さんは、先生について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんは、せんせいについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa, sensei ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: He spends a full hour with every patient.
He's always running late, so his patients end up waiting.
He takes his time and looks at each patient properly.

questions.explanation: Line 2: 'koko no sensei, hitori hitori chanto jikan kakete mite kureru kara'. Jikan o kakeru is choosing to put time into something, here each patient (hitori hitori), properly (chanto). Kenji grumbles jikan kakesugi da yo (line 3, he takes way too long), and at the end he'll eat his snack slowly: jikan kakete, yukkuri taberu (line 18). A mixes it up with line 1: the hour is how long the wait still takes, mada ichijikan mo kakaru, and kakaru is how long something takes. It isn't time per patient. B is wrong: nobody says he's late. The wait is long because he's thorough.

questions.english: Your manager Tanaka-san stayed after work to go through your presentation with you, even though his week is packed. When you're done, he says, "jaa, kyou wa kono gurai ni shimashou ka." Thank him for making time for you, using jikan o toru.
questions.ja: じゃあ、今日はこのぐらいにしましょうか。
questions.kana: じゃあ、きょうはこのぐらいにしましょうか。
questions.romaji: jaa, kyou wa kono gurai ni shimashou ka.
questions.answer: Thank him politely with jikan o toru: ojikan totte itadaite, arigatou gozaimashita (thank you for making time for me). To apologise for taking up his time, use the causative: ojikan torasete shimatte sumimasen.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai. kyou wa ojikan totte itadaite, arigatou gozaimashita.
modelAnswers.ja: はい。今日はお時間取っていただいて、ありがとうございました。
modelAnswers.english: Yes. Thank you for making time for me today.

modelAnswers.romaji: oisogashii tokoro, ojikan torasete shimatte sumimasen. arigatou gozaimashita.
modelAnswers.ja: お忙しいところ、お時間取らせてしまってすみません。ありがとうございました。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry to take up your time when you're so busy. Thank you.

questions.explanation: Kenji says it to Okaasan in line 10: nanka, jikan totte kurete arigatou. She has just said she hardly ever gets time to talk with him (line 9, nakanaka torenai). Jikan o toru is setting time aside, and it's the usual way to thank someone for theirs. With your manager, make it polite with o- and itadaite: ojikan totte itadaite. The apology uses the causative: ojikan torasete (making you take the time). English 'take' can mislead you, though: how long something takes is kakaru, as in mada ichijikan mo kakaru (line 1). Ojikan tsukutte itadaite would also work, if you want to stress that he squeezed you in.

questions.english: Kenta asks, "konshuu, issho ni nanika tabe ni ikanai?" Your week is packed, but next week looks better. Tell him you can make time next week.
questions.ja: 今週、一緒に何か食べに行かない？
questions.kana: こんしゅう、いっしょになにかたべにいかない？
questions.romaji: konshuu, issho ni nanika tabe ni ikanai?
questions.answer: Use jikan o tsukuru in the potential: raishuu nara jikan tsukureru yo (I can make time next week). Saying konshuu wa chotto isogashii kedo first softens the no.

modelAnswers.romaji: konshuu wa chotto isogashii kedo, raishuu nara jikan tsukureru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 今週はちょっと忙しいけど、来週なら時間作れるよ。
modelAnswers.english: This week's a bit busy, but I can make time next week.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, konshuu wa muri. raishuu nara, nantoka jikan tsukuru kara.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今週は無理。来週なら、なんとか時間作るから。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, this week's impossible. I'll find time next week somehow.

questions.explanation: Okaasan uses it three times: nantoka jikan tsukutta (line 8, she managed to make time in a busy week), sekkaku jikan tsukutta n da kara (line 13, I went to the trouble of making time) and raishuu nara, mata jikan tsukureru (line 15, I can make time again next week). 'Make time' really is tsukuru, and as in English it means squeezing time out of a full schedule. Jikan o toru (lines 9-10) is setting it aside. The potential, jikan tsukureru, is how you promise to fit someone in. With a friend, casual is right.

questions.english: There's another hour to wait. What did Okaasan suggest?
questions.ja: お母さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Shall we kill some time at the café across the road?
choices.romaji: mae no kafe de jikan tsubusou ka

choices.english: Shall we murder some time at the café across the road?
choices.romaji: mae no kafe de jikan korosou ka

choices.english: Shall we put some time into the café across the road?
choices.romaji: mae no kafe de jikan kakeyou ka

questions.explanation: Line 4: 'jaa, mae no kafe de jikan tsubusou ka'. Kenji answers nanika tabenagara jikan tsubusou (line 5), and later mou hitotsu tabete, jikan tsubusou kana (line 16). Killing time is tsubusu, 'squash': you squash the empty time flat. B is a word-for-word copy of 'kill time'. Korosu is only for killing living things, so jikan o korosu sounds like a murder plot. C is wrong: jikan o kakeru is putting time into something on purpose, like the doctor with each patient (line 2). Here they just want to fill a wait.
